project.name: sm64ds-decomp
project.title: Super Mario 64 DS
project.language: C++ (real classes, folded into translation units). Legacy one-function files may still be C.
project.compiler: mwccarm 2004/b56 is the canonical, pinned compiler (tools/match.py CANONICAL, tools/rombuild.py VERSION). A few files carry a per-file override in config/rombuild-versions.txt; the 1.2 and other builds are for sweeps only. Build flags (C): -O4,p -enum int -lang c99 -char signed -interworking -proc arm946e -gccext,on -msgstyle gcc -Cpp_exceptions off. Flags (C++): the same with -lang c++ (tools/mangle.py and tools/match.py add it for you; a leading //cpp line selects it in a scratch file). 2004/b56 is not in the 1.2 sweep zip: tools/recover_cw2004.py produces it.
project.cppNote: Real methods are compiler-spelled. Write the class and let mwccarm mangle it: python tools/mangle.py candidate.cpp --expect <symbol> asks the pinned compiler which symbols a source emits. Never hand-spell a _ZN... name or type this as int*. In a scratch file or a legacy one-function file the first line must be exactly //cpp (match.py ignores the extension); a promoted translation unit is a plain .cpp under src/.
project.setup: clone {github} and follow CONTRIBUTING.md (python deps + the 1.2 sweep trio from the DS-decomp Discord + python tools/recover_cw2004.py for the pinned 2004/b56, which is NOT in that zip + tools/unpack.py on YOUR OWN cartridge dump). Details in notes/setup-mwccarm.md.
project.readFirst: AGENTS.md (what a change looks like, the gates, the PR format), notes/cpp-class-form.md (destructor variant order, vtable and RTTI ownership, struct copies, bool widening), notes/tu-promotion-conventions.md (the canonical promotion workflow), notes/src-domain-buckets.md (which src/ directory and file stem), notes/agents/PIPELINE.md and notes/agents/README.md (the v2 fleet protocol: queue claim, independent verification, one integrator), then notes/mwccarm-codegen.md and notes/pret-idioms.md for codegen levers. Read these from the live origin/main, not an old checkout. Coordinate through the v2 queue (MERGE.md section 1); the tangos.dev range-claims service is a separate best-effort fallback, not unified with it.
project.submitting:
Read AGENTS.md in the repo root before you start; if this text and AGENTS.md ever disagree, AGENTS.md wins. The work now is turning matched code into real C++ and folding it into the right translation units (every function is already matched: 11,389 of 11,389). Both halves are required: source that reads like it shipped in 2004 (idiomatic, period-accurate C++), and bytes that match the retail cartridge under 2004/b56. When they conflict, byte accuracy wins because it is the only half a machine can check.
THREE TIERS, three different numbers (python tools/tiers.py): MATCHED (the compiled bytes equal the ROM, 100%), CONVERTED (a person can read it: a real name, no raw offset arithmetic, no unk_ fields, no codegen tricks, calls by real names; this is the one that moves), LINKED (the matched translation unit reaches the PC port). They are not a funnel and have different denominators. A good change raises CONVERTED without moving a single matched byte.
TWO SHAPES of change. (1) A shadow-struct file rewritten as a real C++ class: real member names, real base and vtable, real method calls instead of offset arithmetic and mangled-name free functions, still byte-identical (notes/cpp-class-form.md). (2) A promoted translation unit (a FOLDED TU): once a class's files are all real methods, the one-function files are merged into one genuine .cpp the way the original unit was shaped, verified by a partitioned link, then enrolled with tools/tu_promote.py (notes/tu-promotion-conventions.md). Who matched each function stays in function-authors.json by address; moving a file changes no credit. A brand-new match of a previously unclaimed ROM function still follows the old rule: one function per file, the file name is the symbol, .cpp with //cpp as the first line.
WORKFLOW, class first, C++ from the start. (a) Recover the class: RTTI gives the real name and base (rtti_extract, rom_class_names), vtables give slot order and own overrides (rtti_vtables), tu_map and tu_names give the unit boundary and file stem. (b) Write the header with the real base and virtuals in vtable order; the base comes from RTTI, never guessed from field use. (c) Write the unit .cpp in ROM address order and ask the compiler for names with mangle, never by hand. (d) Iterate a method at a time with match (use --version 2004/b56), but the whole-unit compile is the truth: tubuild_verify (bytes, relocation type and destination), then tubuild_linkcheck. A masked byte match alone can pass a call to the wrong function. (e) Place with srcpath (python tools/srcpath.py <symbol>); do not compose a path, because delinks.txt is written from what srcpath returns and a wrong path silently falls back to ROM bytes. (f) Preview the enrollment with tu_promote_plan (a dry run). Applying it, and the pre-push gates (rombuild, prepush_linkcheck, port_refcheck for renames, check_decl_agreement, romdata_check for owned data), belong to the finishing step in your own worktree, not to a Console button.
Every file in src/ MUST reproduce the ROM bytes (the `validate` CI check) and must not carry a raw asm transcription. A byte pass says nothing about whether the C++ is acceptable: source acceptance is separate, done by someone who did not write it, and recorded in the v2 queue (check_pr_source_review --pr N before landing; there is no CI check for it). Header edits move the codegen of every consumer (python tools/affected_src.py <header> first). Take types from the real headers (#include "common.h") instead of declaring struct bodies locally; the langmode ratchet fails CI on new shadow declarations.
PUBLISHING IS NOT YOURS. Class and translation-unit work lands through the v2 queue: a producer, an independent verifier, and one integrator who owns the order and publishes. Console does not open PRs for this work (autoPr is off for this project). Make local, focused commits in your worktree and hand the exact commit SHA plus the proof to the verifier. A PR title names the classes converted or functions matched; the body carries the proof (the RTTI and vtable evidence for a class-identity claim, the gate results for a promotion); one coherent change; tooling and CI changes go in a separate PR. How PRs are reviewed and merged: MERGE.md. Close-but-not-matching drafts go to nearmiss/db.jsonl via tools/nearmiss_db.py, never to src/. asm bodies are legal only under a HAND-ASM PRIMITIVE or NONMATCHING banner (notes/asm-policy.md).
project.rules: only your own legally dumped ROM; never commit the ROM, its assets, or extracted binaries - the one deliberate exception is the annotated disassembly TEXT of still-unmatched functions, published in the coordination data (chaos-data branch) so contributors can work, the same practice as decomp repos committing .s files; import struct/field knowledge (see CREDITS.md) but write all C from scratch.
project.nearMissNote: If a function will not fully match after real effort, do not discard your best attempt - it is still valuable. Store the closest compiling draft as a near-miss (highest-yield input to the refine tier); most matches now start from someone's stored near-miss. Log tries with tools/log_attempt.py (attempt tree); tip C still in nearmiss/db.jsonl via --src; final how via tools/stamp_provenance.py (not tools/bank.py fan-out).

matchConventions.srcLayout: Promoted translation units are filed by what the class is, under src/game/actors/ (d_a_foo.cpp), src/game/player/, src/game/stages/, src/minigames/, src/runtime/actor/, src/ui/hud/ and src/engine/<subsystem>/ (notes/src-domain-buckets.md). A class with a ROM RTTI name is filed under its snake_case stem (daFoo_c -> d_a_foo.cpp, tools/tu_names.py); a class we coined keeps its class name. Do not compose the path: ask python tools/srcpath.py <symbol> (new files: srcpath.new_path_for(symbol, 'cpp')). Legacy one-function files still sit flat as src/<symbol>.c|.cpp until their unit is promoted.

project.knownWalls: PROVEN unreachable from source (see notes/matching-style.md 'Known walls') - not an excuse to give up, but if your near-miss has collapsed to EXACTLY one of these, verify it, tell the user it's a known wall, and move on/hand to the permuter instead of grinding. (1) FIRST-ACCESS-FOLD: a single read-modify-write through base+offset (x->flag |= BIT) is 'add rN,base,#off; ldr [rN]; op; str [rN]' in the ROM but folds to 'ldr [base,#off]' from ALL C/C++ (array-index/pointer/(int)-cast/volatile/C++ inheritance, -O1..-O4, any version, permuter) - the whole tiny-arm9 flag-setter cluster (WithMeshClsn/BgCh setters, func_020353e0..func_02035784). If your ONLY divergence is that 1-instr materialization, it's the wall. (2) PURE SCHEDULING: same instructions reordered (load/store batching, cond-move polarity), same size, no statement/operand order changes it - the permuter can't flip it either.

GITHUB_TOKEN.note: Read-only GitHub token. Raises the API rate limit (anonymous is 60/hr) so contributor stats and PR-based match attribution work. A fine-grained token with public-repo read access is enough - it is stored encrypted on your machine and never shared.

ANTHROPIC_API_KEY.note: Only if you run the Claude cascade/refine tools over the API instead of driving them from an editor session.

GLM_API_KEY.note: z.ai coding-plan key for the GLM refine tier (tools/glm_refine.py).

DEEPSEEK_API_KEY.note: DeepSeek platform API key. Stored encrypted; gives you a DeepSeek box (deepseek-chat / deepseek-reasoner).

NEMOTRON_API_KEY.note: Local Nemotron-3 via LM Studio (OpenAI-compatible server on localhost:1234, model 'nemo'). The server ignores the value, so any placeholder like 'lm-studio' works - storing it just switches the Nemotron box on and makes it console-drivable. Start LM Studio (Start-Nemotron.ps1) before driving.

REQUESTY_API_KEY.note: Requesty gateway key (rqsty-sk-...). Gives you a Requesty box that runs one free Requesty model (picked via the box's dropdown) through the refine driver. Stored encrypted.

MOONSHOT_API_KEY.note: Moonshot AI key. Gives you a Kimi box driving kimi-k3 (OpenAI-compatible at api.moonshot.ai). Stored encrypted.

OPENAI_API_KEY.note: OpenAI API key. Gives you a GPT box driving gpt-5.6-luna. The effort dropdown maps to reasoning_effort (minimal/low/medium/high). Stored encrypted.

CLAIMS_API_KEY.note: Write key for the tangos.dev claims board. Without it the schedulers still READ claims (so they will not hand you work someone else holds), but they cannot announce yours - which is how two contributors end up grinding the same overlay. Mint a service token at the link below: click "Mint a service token", copy it once (it is shown once and never again), and paste it here. It is claims-scoped - it can lock and release address ranges and nothing else - lasts 30 days, and is revocable from the same page. Locks post under your handle from CLAIMS_HANDLE / tools/claims_handle.txt / your OS username.

requirements.notes: mwccarm (CodeWarrior ARM) + license.dat go in tools/mwccarm/; extract your own legally dumped ROM with tools/unpack.py to produce extracted/. The ROM and extracted binaries are never committed.

categories.label: Progress & Reporting
categories.description: Read-only status: how much of the game is matched.

categories.label: Worklists & Scheduling
categories.description: Pick and order the next functions to attack.

categories.label: Analysis & Debugging
categories.description: Disassemble, diff a candidate against the ROM, study codegen.

categories.label: Matching & Cracking
categories.description: Template/structural/LLM tiers that produce and bank matches.

categories.label: Near-miss & Refine
categories.description: Store, categorize, and finish close-but-not-matching drafts.

categories.label: Verification & Auditing
categories.description: Prove banked matches really reproduce the ROM bytes.

categories.label: Class / TU
categories.description: Convert matched code to real C++ classes and fold it into translation units: placement, compiler-spelled names, whole-unit verify, promotion plan, gates.

tools.label: Progress report
tools.description: Report decomp completion: matched functions and bytes vs the whole game. Use --bar for the committed-data README block (reproducible without the ROM or local ledger).

args.name: bar
args.description: Emit the compact README progress block from committed data only.

tools.label: Progress treemap
tools.description: WinDirStat-style treemap of decomp progress: every function is a rectangle, colored by match status, grouped by module. Writes a self-contained HTML artifact (does not touch repo source).

tools.label: Build worklist
tools.description: Emit a worklist of unmatched functions with fully-resolved context (disasm, callees, pool slots, examples) for an agent to attempt. JSONL to stdout, or --pretty for one readable row.

args.name: module
args.description: Restrict to one module (e.g. arm9, ov006).

args.name: no_template
args.description: Exclude functions a template already handles (the LLM pile).

args.name: easy
args.description: Only straight-line / single-guard functions (high LLM hit rate).

args.name: spread
args.description: Round-robin across all modules, freshest-first, to stay in the high-hit-rate regime.

args.name: similar
args.description: Order by number of already-matched lookalikes (best few-shot examples first).

args.name: random
args.description: Pull unmatched functions uniformly at random (any size), reshuffled every run (the Random role).

args.name: examples
args.description: Attach up to N verified sibling sources as few-shot examples per record (0 disables).

args.name: klass
args.description: Only methods of this C++ class (subsystem batching).

args.name: list_classes
args.description: Print unmatched-function counts per C++ class, then exit.

tools.label: Similarity scheduler
tools.description: Fuzzy opcode-similarity scheduler: order unmatched functions by similarity to already-matched ones for the highest hit rate, attaching the closest matched siblings as scaffolding. --explain NAME shows a function's nearest matched neighbours.

args.name: spread
args.description: Spread the batch across modules/address space.

args.name: explain
args.description: Show the closest matched siblings for one function name.

tools.label: Triage template compliance
tools.description: Classify unmatched functions as strict (exact template match), regperm (only register permutation differs), or none. Surfaces template-correct, regalloc-blocked cheap wins.

tools.label: Recurring shapes
tools.description: Find idioms worth templatizing: shapes the LLM already cracked that still have many unmatched siblings.

args.name: min
args.description: Only shapes with >= N unmatched siblings.

tools.label: Cluster by callees
tools.description: Score unmatched functions by match likelihood and cluster ones sharing callees, for batching under a single agent.

tools.label: Disassemble bytes
tools.description: Quick scratch disassembler for an extracted DS binary to ARM assembly.

args.name: binary
args.description: Path to the extracted binary, e.g. extracted/arm9_dec.bin.

args.name: thumb
args.description: Decode as Thumb instead of ARM.

tools.label: Verify one function or method
tools.description: The oracle for one function: compile a candidate C or C++ file with the pinned mwccarm and relocation-aware byte-compare it to the ROM. Without --version it compiles once with the canonical 2004/b56 (pass --all to sweep every build). A //cpp first line, or a .cpp scratch file marked //cpp, selects C++ with the build's -Cpp_exceptions off. This is the ground-truth verifier for a single function; it does not bank anything. A multi-function translation unit is verified as a unit with tubuild_verify, not with this.

args.name: c
args.description: Path to the candidate C/C++ file (a scratch file for a method of a class, or a legacy src/ file).

args.name: version
args.description: mwccarm version. Use the canonical 2004/b56 (the default the repo builds with); only sweep other builds deliberately.

args.name: all
args.description: Sweep every known mwccarm build instead of the single canonical one.

args.name: module
args.description: Target module: arm9 (default) or an overlay like ov006 - resolves the overlay binary + load address automatically. REQUIRED for overlay functions, or the target reads as empty.

args.name: brief
args.description: Terse pass/fail per version; skips the full byte dump. Use for large functions to keep output small.

args.name: bin
args.description: Advanced: override the target binary path instead of --module resolution.

tools.label: Per-instruction diff
tools.description: Iteration oracle: compile a candidate and show the per-instruction byte diff vs the ROM with relocations wildcarded (offset | target insn | candidate insn | OK/MISMATCH/reloc).

args.name: target_hex
args.description: Target bytes as hex (alternative to module/addr/size).

tools.label: Size-tolerant block diff
tools.description: Aligns mnemonic/operand sequences (branch targets and pc-offsets normalized) to diff a candidate against the ROM even when sizes differ - for cracking large functions incrementally. EXPENSIVE on multi-KB functions (dumps every diverging block); prefer fdiff --quiet first, and pass quiet=true or limit=1-2 on large functions.

args.name: module
args.description: arm9 or an overlay like ov006 (resolves the overlay binary automatically).

args.name: quiet
args.description: Only the aligned block map + summary, no per-instruction dump. Compact.

args.name: limit
args.description: Show per-instruction detail for only the first N diverging blocks (fix the earliest first). Use 1-2 on large functions.

tools.label: Register coloring study
tools.description: Empirical study of when mwccarm colors temporaries into ip/r12, to bias templates.

tools.label: Demangle symbols
tools.description: Pragmatic Itanium C++ demangler: extract class::method and argument types from mangled _Z names.

args.name: names
args.description: One or more mangled names (space separated).

tools.label: Three tiers
tools.description: Report the three independent progress numbers: MATCHED (bytes equal the ROM), CONVERTED (readable C++: real name, no raw offsets, no unk_ fields, no codegen tricks, real call names) and LINKED (the matched unit reaches the PC port). CONVERTED is the one that moves.

tools.label: Where does this symbol live
tools.description: Resolve a symbol to its src/ path. A function folded into a translation unit resolves to that unit's file, so several symbols can share one path. Never compose a src/ path yourself: delinks.txt is written from this tool's answer.

args.name: symbol
args.description: Symbol to look up (the compiler-spelled name for a method).

args.name: index
args.description: Dump the whole symbol-to-path map as JSON.

tools.label: Ask the compiler for symbol names
tools.description: Compiler oracle, not a hand mangler. Compiles a C++ source with the pinned 2004/b56 flags (-lang c++ -Cpp_exceptions off) and lists the symbols it defines, so substitutions, thunks and constructor/destructor variants are the compiler's answer. Use --expect to require an exact symbol.

args.name: file
args.description: C/C++ source with the definitions to compile as C++.

args.name: details
args.description: Also show ELF type, binding and size.

tools.label: Translation-unit map
tools.description: Recover the original translation-unit boundaries the linker erased (build/tu_map.json). With --module and --verbose, lists a module's units and their functions. Needs build/rtti.json and build/rtti_vtables.json first: run rtti_extract, then rtti_vtables with out=build/rtti_vtables.json.

args.name: module
args.description: Analyse one module and print it, e.g. ov045.

tools.label: Unit candidates
tools.description: Candidate translation units from build/tu_map.json with their state (shadow, text-verified, link-verified, promoted).

args.name: module
args.description: Restrict to one module, e.g. ov045.

args.name: verify_sample
args.description: Sample N functions with build_pin.verify (default 5, 0 to skip).

tools.label: Inspect one unit
tools.description: Full detail for one candidate unit: its functions, classes, manifest entry and state.

args.name: id
args.description: Translation-unit id as <module>/<unit>, e.g. ov045/PoleLift (python tools/tubuild.py list shows the candidates).

tools.label: Create a shadow unit
tools.description: Generate a shadow .cpp under src_tu/ plus a manifest entry from the existing one-function sources. Only when no usable candidate exists yet. Writes src_tu/ and config/tu_manifest.d/ (never src/).

args.name: id
args.description: Translation-unit id as <module>/<unit>, e.g. ov045/PoleLift (python tools/tubuild.py list shows the candidates).

tools.label: Compile a unit
tools.description: Compile the unit's shadow .cpp with the pinned toolchain into build/tu/. No byte comparison; use tubuild_verify for that.

args.name: id
args.description: Translation-unit id as <module>/<unit>, e.g. ov045/PoleLift (python tools/tubuild.py list shows the candidates).

tools.label: Verify a whole unit
tools.description: The whole-unit truth: one compile of the unit, then every member's bytes, relocation types and relocation destinations checked against the ROM (match.py, objisolate, reloc_audit). Runs with --no-write, so it never changes the manifest. A masked byte match is not enough; this is the check that catches a call to the wrong function.

args.name: id
args.description: Translation-unit id as <module>/<unit>, e.g. ov045/PoleLift (python tools/tubuild.py list shows the candidates).

tools.label: Link-check a unit
tools.description: Whole-range link in a scratch tree: substitutes the unit and compares the linked module with the ROM. --baseline runs the same pipeline with no substitution (the control that says whether a failure belongs to the unit or the harness); --partitioned and --partial are the other link modes.

args.name: id
args.description: Translation-unit id as <module>/<unit>, e.g. ov045/PoleLift (python tools/tubuild.py list shows the candidates).

args.name: baseline
args.description: Control run with no unit substituted (needs --module).

args.name: partitioned
args.description: Retain N ROM-ordered text entries plus one exact data owner.

args.name: clean
args.description: Delete this unit's scratch tree first.

tools.label: Promotion plan (dry run)
tools.description: Report what promoting a text-verified unit would touch (move the source to its production path, retire the absorbed one-function files, rewrite delinks.txt and the manifest) and change nothing. This entry is a dry run on purpose: tu_promote.py mutates by default, so applying it is done by hand in your own worktree, after tubuild_verify and tubuild_linkcheck, not through Console.

tools.label: Full ROM build and check
tools.description: The pre-push gate: compile every enrolled source, link, and byte-diff every module against the retail ROM (106/106 modules exact, mismatching: 0). Compiled objects are cached by content in build/objcache, so only what a change reaches is recompiled. Writes only build/.

args.name: no_rom
args.description: Link and verify but skip .nds packaging (the usual pre-push form).

args.name: partitioned_tu
args.description: Verify one proven merged unit with the full production gates, e.g. ov002/daObjAbuku_c.

tools.label: Pre-push link check
tools.description: Link-verify the matched src/ files in a commit range, consumers of changed headers included. match.py wildcards relocated words, so a call to the wrong function can match locally and fail CI as WRONG-DEST; this catches it. Inspects commits, not uncommitted edits.

tools.label: Port reference check
tools.description: Check port/'s literal src/ paths and symbol names for references stranded by a rename, a .c to .cpp migration or a file move. No compiler, no ROM, about a second. Run it before pushing anything that renames or moves a src/ or include/ file.

args.name: json
args.description: Write the JSON report to this path.

tools.label: Declaration agreement
tools.description: Do the tree's extern declarations of a symbol agree with its definition? A ratchet: existing disagreements are banked, a new one fails. --changed scopes it to what a branch can have broken. No compiler, no ROM, about twelve seconds. Include the real header instead of copying a declaration.

args.name: changed
args.description: Scan only what this branch can have broken; value is the base (default origin/main).

args.name: symbol
args.description: Print every declaration and definition of one symbol.

args.name: inventory
args.description: Headline counts and the worst offenders.

tools.label: Owned data check
tools.description: Compare the DATA a compiled source emits (vtables, typeinfo, static data) against the cartridge. A measurement, not a pass/fail gate: its exit status is not a verdict, read the per-symbol results and the emitted-symbol coverage. Use it for a unit that owns non-text data.

args.name: files
args.description: The one source to compile without isolation, e.g. src/game/actors/d_a_foo.cpp.

tools.label: Source review evidence
tools.description: Read the queue's independent source-review evidence for a PR: missing evidence, stale review, incomplete coverage and unresolved findings are blockers. Read-only (never publishes). Run immediately before landing a fleet PR.

tools.label: Class graph from RTTI
tools.description: Read the class graph out of the ROM's own RTTI (build/rtti.json): each polymorphic class's original name, vtable and base edges. Ground truth, not inference. The base of a class comes from here, never from field use.

args.name: check
args.description: Fail unless the frozen census reproduces.

tools.label: Vtable slots
tools.description: Read each class's vtable and say which slots are its own code. --own CLASS lists one class's slots in order (the order the header must declare its virtuals).

args.name: fields
args.description: Recover each intermediate's own fields from its own methods.

args.name: out
args.description: Write the JSON here (build/rtti_vtables.json is what tu_map reads).

tools.label: Give RTTI records real symbols
tools.description: Rename the ROM's type_info records and name strings to real symbols (_ZTI/_ZTS). Dry run by default; apply rewrites config/**/symbols.txt.

args.name: include_referenced
args.description: Also rename the deferred ones (does not rewrite src).

tools.label: ROM class names
tools.description: Recover each class's ORIGINAL name from the cartridge's RTTI and say where the decomp's name agrees or was coined. A ROM-named class is filed under its snake_case stem; a coined name stays until the real one is recovered.

tools.label: Candidate file names
tools.description: Candidate original file stems for the ROM's RTTI classes (daFoo_c -> d_a_foo). A naming convention, not a recovered __FILE__.

tools.label: Class index
tools.description: Class-level index of the tree: which classes exist, their methods, and which still have unmatched or near-miss symbols.

args.name: missing
args.description: Only classes with unmatched or near-miss symbols.

tools.label: Language-mode audit
tools.description: Static audit of the C/C++ gap: C++ symbols still built in C mode, hand-spelled mangled names, local shadow struct declarations, inline asm and laundering macros. Reads git-tracked files only, no compiler, no ROM. CI ratchets it.

tools.label: Template sweep (single module)
tools.description: Zero-token template tier: recognize self-contained function shapes (constant returns, field load/store, arithmetic), emit the obvious C, and verify via the oracle. Dry-run by default; --apply banks wins.

tools.label: Template sweep (all modules)
tools.description: Run the free template tier (leaf + reloc rules) across every module. Dry-run by default; --apply records wins and writes src/*.c.

tools.label: Structural clone matcher
tools.description: Free matcher: bank unmatched functions that are byte-identical structural clones of matched ones (modulo relocs), with a reloc-destination gate to prevent false positives. Dry-run by default.

tools.label: Parameterized clone matcher
tools.description: Pair unmatched with matched functions sharing an instruction skeleton, substitute immediates, and re-verify. Compounds with clone. Dry-run by default.

tools.label: Verify & bank fan-out result
tools.description: Independently re-compile and re-check each candidate in a fan-out result JSON, then bank the passing ones. Nothing is trusted on an agent's say-so. Verify-only without --apply. Fan-out verify/bank only — use log_attempt for tries and stamp_provenance for how.

args.name: result
args.description: Path to the fan-out output JSON.

args.name: worklist
args.description: The worklist JSONL the result was produced from.

tools.label: Cheap LLM tier (Haiku)
tools.description: Query a cheap model on template near-misses with the target asm + closest draft, recompile/verify, retry once with diff feedback. The compiler+oracle judge, not the model. --apply records wins.

tools.label: GLM refine driver
tools.description: Run the refine tier through the GLM API instead of Workflow agents: concurrent jobs, up to N attempts per function, early-stop on stale rounds. Writes drafts and appends wins.

args.name: wl
args.description: Refine worklist JSONL (build with refine_wl first).

tools.label: Build refine worklist
tools.description: Export the closest fixable near-misses from the near-miss DB into a refine fan-out worklist, routed by category. Appends attempted addresses to a ledger to avoid repeats.

args.name: include_attempted
args.description: Also schedule near-misses already in the attempted ledger (keeps a driven refiner fed instead of drying up to 1 target after a pass).

tools.label: Near-miss DB stats
tools.description: Summary of the persistent near-miss database (how many stored, divergence distribution).

tools.label: List close near-misses
tools.description: List the closest stored near-misses (the permuter/hand-fix backlog).

tools.label: NONMATCHING stats
tools.description: Stats on parked logic-correct C that cannot byte-match at the compiler tier.

tools.label: Link-verify corpus
tools.description: Reconstruct the linked bytes of each banked match and byte-compare to the ROM with relocations resolved. Verdicts: VERIFIED, WRONG, BLIND-n, NO-REPRO, NO-SYM. For a multi-function unit use tubuild_linkcheck; before a push use prepush_linkcheck.

tools.label: Relocation-destination audit
tools.description: Audit that every banked match's relocations point at the correct callees/globals (catches wrong-table false positives the byte-gate wildcards).

tools.label: Verify mangled templates
tools.description: Batch-verify that cleaned-up mangled template functions still byte-match. Optional name substring filter.

args.name: filter
args.description: Only verify names matching this substring.

tools.label: Generate Atlas data
tools.description: CI-safe Chaos Viewer / tangOS Atlas data generator: rebuild the normalized function/progress DB from committed data only (no ROM).

tools.label: Check work claims
tools.description: Read-only check of the coordination claim service for a module/address span (works without an API key).

tools.label: Claim a work span
tools.description: Claim a module/address span on the coordination service so no other agent grinds it. Posts under your handle using the console's CLAIMS_API_KEY - you never handle the key. Without a key configured it returns 401. Returns the claim id; release it when done.

args.name: module
args.description: arm9 or an overlay like ov006.

args.name: note
args.description: Short note, e.g. the function name you're matching.

tools.label: Release a work claim
tools.description: Release a claim you hold (by id, from claims_lock) once the work is banked or abandoned. Uses the console's key + your handle.

args.name: id
args.description: The claim id returned by claims_lock.

tools.label: Import verified symbols
tools.description: Conservatively import verified symbol names from external references into config symbols.txt (never overwrites existing names). Dry-run without --apply.

tools.label: Unpack a DS ROM
tools.description: Unpack a Nintendo DS ROM (.nds) into extracted ARM9/ARM7 binaries, overlays, and filesystem. Requires your OWN legally dumped cartridge; the ROM and its output are never committed.

tools.label: Log attempt
tools.description: REQUIRED after every try. AI: model+reasoning+harness. near_miss --src → nearmiss tip. Not tools/bank.py fan-out.

args.name: status
args.description: matched | near_miss | no_progress | compile_error | failed | skipped.

tools.label: Stamp provenance
tools.description: After MATCH: final how-record. Not a new try. Not tools/bank.py fan-out.

tools.label: Land a drive's results
tools.description: Bank a finished drive: matched sources into src/, near-misses ingested into the DB, free-tier clone/paramclone post-pass, linkcheck gate over everything banked. Stops before git commit/push - that stays a reviewable step.

args.name: no_claims
args.description: Skip claiming the landed address ranges. Console sets this when no claims key is available.
